A tight pressure gradient will reside across the area through the week with a prolonged gusty NE flow. Expect mainly dry conditions from Tuesday night into Thursday with rain chances coming up at the end of the week with the potential for a deepening coastal low to approach the area.

.KEY MESSAGE 3...

As previously discussed the area will reside between an anomalously strong high to the north and a broad area of low pressure off the Mid Atlantic and Southeast coasts. Late in the week, offshore low pressure interacts with mid latitude energy, rapidly deepening in the Thursday to Friday timeframe. The 06Z operational GFS which was an outlier with the other globals and its own ensemble, now is getting some support from the 12Z ECMWF and EC-AIFS in retrograding the deepening low toward the forecast area. However, there is still little support from the ensembles and the AIGFS at this time. It's complex with the interaction of multiple streams in the polar jet. Definitely something to watch, especially with a prolonged period of NE flow and increasing astronomical tides. High surf, dangerous rips currents, beach erosion, and coastal flooding are all on the table, but much too early to have specific details.

FXUS61 KOKX 210311
AFDOKX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
1111 PM EDT Sun Sep 20 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Gale watch posted for the ocean waters with the potential for 
NE gales from Tuesday through the end of the week.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Periods of rain, mainly light, will come to end from NW to 
SE tonight with a cold frontal passage. 

2) A frontal wave is expected to bring another chance of rain 
to the area Monday night to Tuesday along with gusty NE winds. 

3) A prolonged period of NE gales is possible, especially on 
the ocean waters, from Tuesday through the end of the week.
There is the potential for high surf, dangerous rip currents,
and beach erosion.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
High pressure trying to build in from the north will nudge a
frontal boundary south and east during the overnight hours. 
Light rain and drizzle still lingering primarily over the 
southern zones, but should end by daybreak in most areas.

Behind the cold front, northerly winds increase late tonight 
with the potential for gusts up to 20 mph. This will persist 
through the first half of Monday before briefly falling off. 
There will be some partial clearing Monday, mainly across the 
Lower Hudson Valley and Connecticut. Model time-height cross 
sections showing a fair amount of mid and high level clouds. 

Lows tonight will be on the warmer side in the mid 50s to lower
60s due to the cloud cover and winds picking up. Highs will 
through will be close to 5 degrees below normal in the mid 60s 
to lower 70s.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
An anomalously strong high north of the Great Lakes will build
east through the week, bleeding south into the Northeast. At 
the same time, another frontal wave will emerge from the Ohio 
Valley Monday night, tracking to the south of the area. The 
question is the strength of the high and how far the rain shield
will get into the area. The timing for the rain would be late 
Monday night into Tuesday afternoon, the drying out from north 
to south. The best chance for rain will near the NYC/NJ metro, 
falling off to the north and east. There is decent frontogenetic
support. The GFS is the more aggressive of the models in 
bringing some moderate rain across southern portions of the 
forecast area with amounts around half an inch or so. There will
be a tight gradient from rain to nothing. Thus, this is a low 
confidence forecast right now. 

A tight pressure gradient will reside across the area through
the week with a prolonged gusty NE flow. Expect mainly dry 
conditions from Tuesday night into Thursday with rain chances 
coming up at the end of the week with the potential for a 
deepening coastal low to approach the area.

.KEY MESSAGE 3...
As previously discussed the area will reside between an 
anomalously strong high to the north and a broad area of low 
pressure off the Mid Atlantic and Southeast coasts. Late in the
week, offshore low pressure interacts with mid latitude energy,
rapidly deepening in the Thursday to Friday timeframe. The 06Z 
operational GFS which was an outlier with the other globals and 
its own ensemble, now is getting some support from the 12Z 
ECMWF and EC-AIFS in retrograding the deepening low toward the 
forecast area. However, there is still little support from the 
ensembles and the AIGFS at this time. It's complex with the 
interaction of multiple streams in the polar jet. Definitely 
something to watch, especially with a prolonged period of NE 
flow and increasing astronomical tides. High surf, dangerous 
rips currents, beach erosion, and coastal flooding are all on 
the table, but much too early to have specific details.

&&

.AVIATION /03Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
High pressure slowly builds into the region from the north as a
weak wave of low pressure departs east.

Low confidence category forecast through at least the pre-dawn
hours, but generally MVFR heading into the Monday morning push,
but VFR probably prevails at least in the city terminals by 12z.
Improving flight categories elsewhere Monday morning with all
terminals VFR by noon. Light rain during the pre-dawn hours 
may temporarily reduce vsbys below 6sm. 

N winds increase to 10-15G20-25kt after about 12Z Mon, then 
diminish late in the afternoon. 

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...
Chance that VFR prevails for the rest of the night, but also a
chance that cigs are reduced at least temporarily to IFR before
08-09z.


.OUTLOOK FOR 00Z TUESDAY THROUGH THURSDAY...

Monday night: VFR. 

Tuesday through Thursday: Chance of MVFR or lower in showers. 
NE wind gusts 20-25 kt Tuesday and 20-30 kt Wednesday and 
Thursday, highest at the coastal terminals.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
SCA is in effect for the ocean waters out to 20 nm from Monday
into Tuesday, followed by a gale watch Tue night. The gale watch
goes up on the outermost ocean zones (out 20 to 60 nm) beginning
Tue afternoon. 

An anomalously strong high building across eastern Canada this
week and low pressure off the Mid Atlantic and Southeast 
coasts will result in a prolonged period of strong NE flow from 
Tuesday through the end of the week. There could be a prolonged 
period of gales on the ocean waters and possibly the eastern 
non-ocean waters, especially late in the week depending on the 
magnitude and track of a coastal low. There is even a small 
chance at this time for storm force gusts. Preference at this 
time was to back off on the higher wind gusts of the NBM based 
on latest model soundings and model consensus absent the NBM 
bias correction. 

Rip Currents: The rip current risk should remain moderate 
through Monday. Combined seas will build to near 5 ft on Monday,
with some long period 2-ft SE swell. 

Strengthening NE flow and building seas will likely produce a
high rip current risk and high surf, possibly as early as Tue
and definitely from Wed through at least Sat. As ocean swells 
gradually increase to 10-15 ft with periods of about 10-11 
seconds, would expect surf heights to become at least half that
high given a more longshore current vs direct 
onshore trajectory.
